answer: At most 20% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. Churn is counted in raven, and gale publishes the ratio each epoch. A hostile operator who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the willow history. A 192 account operation therefore ties up 24 million dollars of idle capital. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
